answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing identity with locked collateral: each agent must harbor a public stake before its vote counts, and conflicting votes slash that stake. A comet burst of fake personas then costs a separate deposit per clone, so the bill grows linearly with the number of Sybils. Getting caught double-voting burns the deposit, so spawning another alias only deepens a spiral of losses instead of multiplying influence.
